svg.title: Dataflow Gen2 Low-Code Transformation Flow
svg.desc: A flow diagram showing how Dataflow Gen2 connects to sources, applies Power Query transformations, executes scale-out work on managed SQL staging, writes multiple destinations, and integrates with pipeline orchestration.
svg.text: Dataflow Gen2: Low-Code Transformation & Staging Architecture
Power Query Authoring · Managed SQL Scale-Out Staging · Multi-Destination Publishing · Pipeline Orchestration

g.title: Source connectors — Dataflow Gen2 connects Power Query to Fabric, cloud, and on-premises sources.
g.text: Hundreds of native connectors connecting Power Query to diverse data estates
• On-premises & VNet isolation supported via On-Premises & VNet Data Gateways
• Automatic schema discovery, column type inference & preview sampling
• OAuth2, Service Principal, Database Authentication, and Windows Kerberos supported.
• Power Query Privacy Levels (Public, Organizational, Private) isolate cross-source queries.
• Credential ownership bound to connection definitions in Fabric Settings.

g.title: Power Query shaping — Authors define joins, cleansing, types, and aggregations as applied steps.
g.text: Visual M language transformation editor with step-by-step evaluation
• 300+ graphical transformations generate versioned Power Query M formulas
• Dynamic parameterization enables environment switching (Dev ➔ Test ➔ Prod)
• Foldable steps translate directly into native SQL executed at source server.
• Non-folding steps (e.g. complex regex) hand off to Fabric Managed SQL Staging.
Visual validation flags folding barriers before publishing to production.

g.title: Managed SQL staging — Fabric provisions internal staging items for scale-out Dataflow processing.
g.text: Internal Fabric SQL Warehouse compute backing scale-out transformations
• Extracted source data is staged in high-speed Delta Parquet storage
• Downstream merges, large joins & aggregations execute via distributed T-SQL
• Accelerates transformations by up to 10x compared to single-threaded Mashup engine
• Staging items are completely managed by the Fabric service runtime.
• Users must NOT directly modify, query, or rely on internal staging tables.
• Staging compute draws Capacity Units (CUs) from the workspace's assigned capacity.
Enables massive parallel scaling for heavy Power Query transformations.

g.title: Configured destinations — One dataflow can write transformed output to multiple Fabric or external destinations.
g.text: Simultaneous multi-destination writing with schema enforcement
• Replace: Drops and recreates destination table schema on every run.
• Append: Adds new rows to existing table (ensure source deduplication).
• Single dataflow query can branch to multiple destinations in parallel.
Warning: Incorrect Replace mode on production tables overwrites existing historical rows!

g.title: Pipeline orchestration — A pipeline schedules the dataflow and coordinates downstream activities.
g.text: Data Factory Pipeline Orchestration & Operational Coordination
Enterprise scheduling, parameterization, dependency gating, and failure alerting
• Upstream dependency gating via completion signals
• Pass execution date, batch IDs & runtime filters
• Environment variables for CI/CD deployment pipelines
• Reusable dataflow templates across multiple entities
• Automated retry policies on transient network faults
• Real-time Hub & Monitoring hub run status
• Gated downstream Power BI Direct Lake refresh
Always execute Dataflow Gen2 as a step inside a Data Factory Pipeline rather than setting a schedule directly on the Dataflow.
This provides centralized retry handling, parameter injection, and synchronizes downstream Spark or Power BI semantic model refreshes.

svg.text: Fabric Atlas — Original Infographic, August 2026. Grounded in Microsoft Fabric Dataflow Gen2 Specs.
